- Overestimate prices after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is bullish (1.00) in the prior 3–5 days.  
- Underestimate prices when sentiment turns bearish (−1.00) after a recent peak, particularly if the prior 5 days show strong bullish sentiment.  
- Model tends to overreact to short-term sentiment shifts; dampen forecast slopes when sentiment flips abruptly.  
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 10–20% unless sentiment remains bullish.  
- Overshoot correction: if forecast exceeds true outcome by >5% for 2+ consecutive days, reduce next-day forecast by 5–10% to avoid overcorrection.  
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts often overestimate early in the window; cap forecast at 10% above 14-day moving average for first 7 days.
